benchmark.title: The held-out benchmark
benchmark.text: Every delineation method is scored on the same tiles with the same metrics: pixel-pooled IoU, F1, precision and recall over valid pixels, the per-tile mean IoU, and boundary F1 at 2 pixels. Validation chooses the spectral-angle threshold and nothing else; test and catalog tiles are reported as they come, and every catalog site was held out of training. The worse arm is what the documentation quotes.
benchmark.haze: IoU under added haze (reflectance added to every band)
benchmark.missing: No benchmark is shipped with this build yet: the models are still training. The table appears when models/benchmark.json lands.

data.title: Data
data.lede: Every source Rajo reads, its license, and the two data contracts between the offline bake and this page.

sources.title: Sources, probed and licensed
sources.text: Every row was probed live on 2026-09-02 with a browser-like Origin header. "Browser: yes" means the response carried CORS for a static page, which is what lets the app read the data directly; sources without CORS are read by the offline bake only.
sources.rejected: Rejected sources, and why: Esri World Imagery (the legacy tile service is in mature status and the replacement needs an account and an API key); the GRID-Arendal Global Tailings Portal (download requires permission); the Copernicus DEM and Landsat read live in the browser (no CORS, token plumbing), both baked offline instead.

facts.title: Facts the bake relies on
facts.s2: Sentinel-2 L2A surface reflectance is (DN + BOA_ADD_OFFSET) / 10000 with BOA_ADD_OFFSET = -1000 from processing baseline 04.00; Earth Search items carry scale 0.0001 and offset -0.1 on the reflectance assets; DN 0 is no data. Scene classification: 0 no data, 1 saturated or defective, 3 cloud shadow, 8 and 9 cloud, 10 thin cirrus are invalid; 11 is snow or ice.
facts.landsat: Landsat Collection 2 surface reflectance is DN x 0.0000275 - 0.2; QA_PIXEL bits 0 fill, 1 dilated cloud, 2 cirrus, 3 cloud, 4 cloud shadow, 5 snow. Landsat 5 to 2011, Landsat 7 as the 2012 bridge (scan-line gaps composited from the next dates of the season), Landsat 8 and 9 from 2013.
facts.terrarium: Terrarium decoding: elevation in metres = R x 256 + G + B / 256 - 32768. The per-site Copernicus tiles use the same encoding at zooms 10 to 13.
facts.qa: Quality masks flag the mine itself: on a Landsat 5 scene the archive rates 0.0% cloudy, the QA mask still flagged 10.7% of a 24 km window and 69% of those pixels lay inside the mining polygons (bright benches read as cloud, pit floors as shadow). Frames render from every pixel with data; the QA verdict is kept per pixel for the analysis lanes; a scene is accepted when its scene-level cloud cover is at most 2% and 85% of the window is QA-clear, flagged qa_flagged.

contracts.title: The two data contracts
contracts.ingestion: Contract 1, ingestion: data/examples/sites.json declares each site (id, names, ISO3 country, categories, seed, window in km, first year, season months, facts with a source URL). The catalog stage refuses a seed farther than 3 km from a reference polygon, a window outside 4 to 40 km, a fact without a source or a category outside the vocabulary, and writes the site grid (a UTM window whose width is a multiple of three, so the 30 m Landsat grid nests inside the 10 m one) and the reference polygons.
contracts.artifact: Contract 2, artifact: every stage writes a JSON side-car and the export stage assembles one manifest per site with the bytes and sha256 of every file plus the catalog index. The validate stage re-reads everything and refuses a missing file, a drifted hash, a year without a frame or a recorded reason, a series that names a year without a frame, or two engine versions in one tree. Text artifacts are LF on every platform and hashed as stored.
contracts.guards: The same contract is mirrored in the app (contract.ts), so the web reads only what a manifest declares; the artifact guard runs in CI and before every deploy, which then checks the live title, catalog and a deep link.

catalog.title: The catalog as baked
catalog.text: {{sites}} sites in the catalog, {{frames}} yearly frames on disk. A site without frames is one whose bake has not landed yet; a gap is a year with a recorded reason (no scene under 60% cloud inside the season window in either archive, or every candidate failed to read).
catalog.note: Chips, checkpoints and the venv never ship; the site serves the committed artifacts and reads the archives live.

about.title: About
about.lede: What Rajo is, what it is not, who built it and why.
body: Rajo ("open pit" in Chilean Spanish) is an open observatory of the great open-pit mines and lithium evaporation ponds of the world as seen from satellites over four decades. It shows each site on a 3D globe with real relief, replays a yearly time-lapse from 1985 (Landsat) to today (Sentinel-2), computes spectral and mineral indices live in your browser from the raw cloud-optimized GeoTIFFs, runs a learned mine-footprint segmentation in the browser, detects change points on the mined-area signal, and shows where and how much rock moved between the 2000 and the 2011 to 2015 global elevation models. Chilean copper is the core of the catalog; the world's icons are the context.

Everything runs in the browser or comes from a baked, checksummed artifact. There is no backend, no account, and nothing is uploaded anywhere. Every number on screen traces to a computation you can rerun or to a named, dated source.

Rajo is a CAOS project by Felipe Santibanez-Leal: a public, open-source showcase of remote sensing, image processing, signal processing and learned models applied to mining, built to the same standards as the rest of the CAOS product line (shared data contracts, gates by use, bilingual documentation, deep repositories).
about.lifecycleTitle: How it was designed and built
lifecycle: Research first: every data source probed live for CORS, range reads and licence; the methods surveyed against their primary papers (thirty-five DOIs resolved); the concept, the sites and the deploy target decided from that research and persisted as dated dossiers.
A plan with five axes (status, plan, backlog, history, findings) covering the whole product, validated before implementation.

The two data contracts, then the staged offline bake (catalog, scenes, frames, masks, series, dense, dem, export, validate), run detached and in parallel, with a harvest that refuses an incomplete site.
The learned models trained on the Jasansky et al. 2024 tiles with every catalog site held out, exported to ONNX with parity gates, and scored on the same held-out tiles as the classical methods.

The web app built unit by unit, each with its code, its tests, its gate by use and its documentation in the same commit; the architecture modal and the Methods and Data pages transcribed from the persisted research, never recalled from memory.
A static deploy with an atomic release swap and a live content check; versioning by X.XX.XXX with a changelog and a tag per release.
rules: A stretch, a threshold, a penalty or an angle is printed next to the picture it produced; nothing is hidden behind a default.
A year without a frame carries its reason; a cloudy envelope is a null in every series, never an interpolated value.
Areas and volumes are measured inside the reference envelope (the mining polygons dilated by one kilometre); a mask over the whole window would measure the desert.
Learned models report held-out scores on tiles that never touched a catalog site; the worse arm is what the documentation quotes.
Every method names its lane: live in the browser, baked offline, or both; the app never mislabels what it is doing.
Licences travel with the data: the per-site polygons stay CC BY-SA 4.0; Copernicus, USGS, EOX and OpenFreeMap strings are rendered verbatim.

instrument.title: Instrument
instrument.idle: Loads the newest Sentinel-2 scene over this window (last 150 days, under 25% cloud) straight from the cloud-optimized GeoTIFFs into your browser. Nothing is uploaded.

otsu.title: Otsu on the bare-soil index
otsu.text: The threshold that maximises the between-class variance of the BSI histogram, then not-vegetation, not-water, a 3 x 3 opening and small-component removal.

kmeans.title: k-means on the spectra
kmeans.text: Standardised six bands plus NDVI and MNDWI, k-means++ seeding, Lloyd iterations, deterministic seed; clusters ordered from dark to bright.
kmeans.spectrum: Centroid spectrum (B, G, R, NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2)

sam.title: Spectral angle mapper
sam.text: The angle between each pixel spectrum and an endmember; illumination-invariant, so pit walls in shadow still match.
sam.endmemberRef: Endmember: mean spectrum of the reference mining polygons on this scene.
sam.endmemberBare: Endmember: the brightest bare quartile of this scene (no reference polygons on the grid).

instrument.findNote: Classical delineations of disturbed land on one scene, and two learned ones; none of them is ore. Areas are compared with the reference polygons when the site has them.

learned.title: Learned delineation
learned.text: Two models trained offline on the Jasansky et al. 2024 tiles run here on the same scene: a random forest on sixteen per-pixel features, and a U-Net on the six bands. This site was never in their training set.
learned.neverSeen: Every catalog site was held out of training and validation, so this number is not in-sample.
learned.missing: No model files are shipped with this build.

ndvi.name: NDVI, vegetation
ndvi.caveat: Bare pits and dumps sit near zero; irrigated fields and riparian strips light up.

ndwi.name: NDWI, open water
ndwi.caveat: Bright salt crusts can mimic water in NDWI; compare with MNDWI.

mndwi.name: MNDWI, water vs bright crust
mndwi.caveat: Separates ponds and brine from bright salt and tailings better than NDWI.

ndbi.name: NDBI, built-up and bare
ndbi.caveat: Bare rock, dumps and plants all score high: built-up is not mine.

bsi.name: BSI, bare soil
bsi.caveat: The workhorse of the classical masks; deserts are bare everywhere, so the threshold matters.

nbr.name: NBR, burn and moisture
nbr.caveat: Low over dry bare rock; used here as a dryness contrast, not as a burn index.

iron.name: Iron oxide ratio
iron.caveat: Ferric oxides (hematite, goethite) raise the ratio; oxidised dumps and leach pads too. A group indicator, not a mineral map.

clay.name: Clay and hydroxyl ratio
clay.caveat: Al-OH and Mg-OH minerals absorb near 2.2 um and raise the ratio; Sentinel-2 has two SWIR bands, so this is coarse.

ferrous.name: Ferrous minerals ratio
ferrous.caveat: Ferrous iron lowers the NIR; responds to fresh rock and dark dumps.

series.title: Signal lane
series.showMask: show the mask of the year
series.hoverHint: Hover for values; click a year to move the timeline
series.indexNote: Yearly envelope means of NDVI, MNDWI and BSI from the same frames; Landsat years shaded.

flags.cross_sensor: Landsat years are outside the forest training domain (cross-sensor)

relief.none: No elevation difference is baked for this site yet.
relief.epochText: The 3D relief and hillshade come from the global terrain tiles (the year-2000 radar surface in South America) or from the Copernicus surface of 2011 to 2015 baked for this window.
relief.deltaText: Copernicus minus SRTM on the 30 m grid, geoid-corrected and de-biased on stable ground; blue where the ground went down, red where it went up.
relief.showDelta: drape the difference on the map
relief.envelopeNote: Volumes count cells beyond the threshold inside the reference polygons dilated by 1 km; both surfaces are radar surface models and the interval is a single decade.

flags.stable_ground_includes_slopes: too few flat stable cells: slopes included in the noise floor

relief.profileText: Pick two points on the map: both surfaces are sampled from the terrain tiles in your browser along the line.
relief.outsideWindow: the line lies outside the baked Copernicus window
